ac.description: EX2200-C-12P-2G - 12 PoE+ ports and two dual-purpose uplinks, built-in AC supply, fanless, 100 W for PoE (Table 3).

description: Juniper EX2200-C-12P is the compact, fanless member of the EX2200 line: a 1RU-high Gigabit Ethernet access switch 269 mm wide with 12 10/100/1000BASE-T ports, all with PoE+ and 100 W available, and two dual-purpose uplink ports, each an RJ-45 port beside an SFP port of which only one is active at a time. The front carries the 12 jacks in two stacked rows numbered 0 to 11 (the upper jack of a column takes the even number), the two dual-purpose uplinks numbered 0 and 1, a USB port, the management Ethernet port with the RJ-45 console port above it, a mini-USB console port, two chassis status lamps, four port-mode lamps and a Factory Reset/Mode button. The rear carries the earthing terminal, an ESD point, a heatsink and the AC power cord inlet; there are no fans. The power supply is built into the chassis, so there are no bays. The EX2200-C-12T is the same front without PoE.

airflow.note: the cooling system consists of the vents on the top and sides of the chassis and, on PoE+ models, the heatsink in the rear panel; there are no fans, so the chassis is passive.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Hardware guide, Power Supply in EX2200 Switches: "The power supply in EX2200 switches is built in along the rear panel of the chassis"; Table 4 lists "Built-in power supply" and, for the fan, "EX2200-C switches are fanless models". Nothing in the guide describes removing or replacing the supply. It is part of the chassis, not a bay and not a component, and there are no fans.

chassis.note: Table 5: height 1.75 in (4.4 cm), width 10.6 in (26.92 cm) and 19 in (48.26 cm) with the mounting brackets attached, depth 9.4 in (23.8 cm) for the EX2200-C-12P, weight 6.4 lb (2.9 kg). 269.2 x 44.45 x 238.0 is carried: width and depth as the printed metric and the height as the 1U pitch (1.75 in), the printed 4.4 cm being that rounded down. The figures show the end caps inside the width and no ears.

colour.note: borrowed - the chassis #919599 and the jack shell #b1b2b5 are the EX2300 front photograph's medians. The guide's figures are line drawings with no colour and no EX2200-C photograph is held, so these are a relative's and not a reading of this device.

front-console.note: estimated - the mini-USB console port (Figure 3, callout Mini USB port, printed CON) is drawn as chassis art, an 8.6 x 5.1 mm shell with its opening, read off the figure. It is not a component: the library has no mini-USB receptacle and its DCIM export has no row for one. The RJ-45 console port is a component and exports. The guide says one console port is active at a time, the RJ-45 by default.

front-layout.note: estimated - read off Figure 3 as described under gate-1. The 12 jacks stand in one shell of six columns, the first jack at 8.1 mm and a pitch of 15.75 mm (the figure's; the registry's 13.97 is for ganged blocks that abut and the jacks here stand apart, their width reading the registry's 12.7), the rows 14.85 mm apart and the upper row turned 180 so its lamp tabs are above. Each dual-purpose uplink is an RJ-45 jack (105.9 and 149.2 mm) 43.3 mm from an SFP cage (centres 137.1 and 180.4 mm), the pair joined by a printed bracket carrying its number, and between them a column of four triangular lamps with LINK and ST legends (Figure 3, Figure 13). The USB port is upright (turned 90). The console and management jacks are one stacked housing, the console jack above and its keyway up, the management jack below with MGMT printed under it. The mini-USB console port (CON) is chassis art. The figure draws no ESD point on the front. The Juniper logo and the Running Junos mark are not drawn; both have a reserved logo zone. The chassis and shell colours are borrowed (see colour).

gate-1.note: Figure 3 was rendered at 600 dpi and measured with a pixel ruler. Its front face is 2801 px across and 445 px down: 10.41 px per mm across from the 269.2 mm of Table 5 and 10.01 down from 44.45 mm, a 4 percent aspect error, so x and y are each taken from their own dimension and every position is estimated and good to about a millimetre. The jack width reads 12.7 mm, the registry's 12.7 for the ganged RJ-45 cell, on a quantity the scale never saw. The figure is a perspective view from slightly above and its front face is the near rectangle. Figure 6 (rear) is a perspective view too: its face is 2304 px across and 360 down, 8.56 px per mm across and 8.10 down, a 5 percent aspect error.

lamps.note: Hardware guide, Tables 6 to 10 and Figures 8, 10 and 13. Each RJ-45 port has two lamps, Link/Activity and Status, on the tabs of the jack (Figure 11); each dual-purpose uplink has two pairs of lamps, LINK and ST, one pair for each of its two ports (Figure 13), drawn as triangles pointing at their port: the pair pointing right is taken as the SFP port's and the pair pointing left as the RJ-45 port's, which the guide does not state, so it is estimated. The management port has a LINK and an ST lamp beside it, and no lamp in the jack (Figure 10). The Status lamps read out whichever of speed (SPD), duplex (DX), administrative status (EN) and PoE the Factory Reset/Mode button has selected, shown by which port-mode lamp is lit. The jack lamps keep the component's link and activity vocabulary because a block cannot override it per lamp.

mode-lamps-nonpoe.note: the guide lists 4 port status mode LEDs on the PoE+ model and 3 on the non-PoE one; the EX2200-C-12T drawing (Figure 4) nonetheless prints the PoE legend and lamp. This model is the PoE one and carries four.

port-numbering.note: drawing - Figure 3 prints each column's two numbers under its shell, the even number up and left and the odd number down and right (0 and 1, 2 and 3, ... 10 and 11), and the two uplinks 0 and 1 in their brackets. Which jack takes which is by analogy with the EX2300 faceplate (the upper jack takes the even number), estimated. The even numeral is drawn 2.05 mm left of its jack's centre and the odd one 2.05 mm right of it; the figure puts the even one 1.55 mm left and the odd one 0.65 mm right (8.15 for the two-digit 11), and the drawn offsets are the smallest that keep each legend plainly off the centre it would otherwise nearly share and keep 10 and 11 apart. Port numbers are as printed, from 0. The Junos interface names are not printed: Table 4 gives PIC 0 as 12x10/100/1000BASE-T and PIC 1 as 2x 10/100/1000BASE-T or GE SFP, i.e. ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/11 and ge-0/1/0 and ge-0/1/1; they are recorded here and not in an interfaces block because the faceplate does not print them.

power.note: Table 11: maximum power consumed by the switch 30 W when no PoE power is drawn, 102.3 BTU/hour, and maximum PoE power available 100 W; Table 12: AC input 100 through 240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 7 A at 100 VAC and 2.9 A at 230 VAC for switches with ports equipped for PoE.

rear-layout.note: estimated - positions read off Figure 6 as described under gate-1: the oblong slotted plate at the left (about 22 x 6 mm, drawn as a plain darker plate; the slot itself is not cut through), the two earthing holes 20 mm apart with the earth symbol over the second, the finned heatsink from 51.7 to 209.3 mm with one screw beside it, the AC inlet at 238.4 mm centre with its two-line legend (100-120V and 2.2A, 200-240V and 1.0A, as the figure prints; Table 12 gives 7 A and 2.9 A for PoE switches generally, a different thing, and is carried in the attributes), and the ESD symbol over the ESD point at the right. The heatsink is drawn as a solid finned block, a plain darker plate and not a vent, because Figure 6 shows a solid block and the guide says EX2200-C switches have no exhaust openings, so nothing is cut through the rear; the fin slots are not drawn. The serial number ID label (an empty rounded rectangle in the figure) is a paper label carrying a real serial number and is not drawn.

sources.note: EX2200 and EX2200-C Switches Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2022-02-02 (268 pages), the copy held in Juniper's EX documentation archive (https://www.juniper.net/documentation/en_US/release-independent/downloads/ex-series/ex-series-doc-archives.zip, member ex-series-doc-archives/ex2200.pdf): Figure 3 (EX2200-C PoE+ front), Figure 6 (rear with heatsink), Table 3 (models), Table 5 (chassis size and weight), Tables 6 to 10 (LEDs and Figures 8, 10 and 13), the cooling system section, Tables 11 and 12 (power) and Table 16 (environment). The guide is the only source held for the EX2200-C: Juniper's datasheet is dehosted, the held photograph set has no EX2200 or EX2200-C photograph and the maker's image library no longer carries one. The guide carries Juniper's copyright and reserves its rights, so its figures were read for what is on each face and where, and none was copied; every skin here is drawn from those measurements.

uplinks.note: drawing - two dual-purpose uplink ports numbered 0 and 1, each an RJ-45 port and an SFP port of which only one can be active at a time (Uplink Ports; Table 4 gives 2x 10/100/1000BASE-T or GE SFP). The RJ-45 port is a placement in the uplink-rj45 group and the SFP port one in the uplink-sfp group, so each exports as its own interface. Figure 3 draws the SFP port as a rectangular opening with a stepped lower edge, taken as an SFP cage.
